To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Sin3a complex acts as a context dependent ISGF3/ STAT3 transcriptional switch.

1) STAT3 transcriptional activation is controlled by regulated acetylation, 2) Sin3a is a novel, negative regulator of the STAT3 transcriptional program, 3) Sin3a acts as a contextdependent switch for STAT3 versus ISGF3 transcription and, 4) Sin3a and the HDAC complex are essential for IFN-mediated ant-viral defense.

Sin3a is a novel STAT3-interacting protein that is required for IFN-dependent STAT transcriptional activity, but is dispensable for STAT3-dependent gene transcription induced by other stimuli, such as IL6.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel regulators of STAT3 and ISGF3 transcription and their role in the regulation of the IFN response.
the role of the histone deacetylases (HDACs) in regulating STAT transcriptional activity.
the role of the Sin3 complex as a transcriptional repressor and activator of STAT proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Sin3a is a STAT3 repressor and a positive regulator of the ISGF3 complex, and that its activity is regulated by acetylation of STAT3.
the Sin3a transcriptional complex is a key player in the control of IFNa-dependent STAT3 transcription.
Sin3a is a key regulator of the IFN response, acting as a transcriptional repressor of STAT3-dependent gene transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
STAT3 transcriptional activation is controlled by regulated acetylation, and Sin3a is a critical player in the control of this process.
the STAT3-dependent transcriptional program is repressed in IFN-stimulated cells through a Sin3a-dependent mechanism.
the STAT3/ISGF3 transcriptional switch is controlled by a Sin3a/ HDAC complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
STAT3 transcriptional activation is controlled by regulated, context-dependent deacetylation.
STAT3 and ISGF3 can be differentially activated by the same stimuli, in the same cell, and this differential response depends on Sin3a.
the transcriptional activity of STATs is controlled by regulated acetylation/deacetylation and that this regulation is context-dependent, depending on the STAT complex activated and on the cell type.
